log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 50% BRING: rotom, 22% BRING: torterra, 20% BRING: torkoal
Pick 2: 45% BRING: torterra, 34% BRING: torkoal, 10% BRING: scrafty
Pick 3: 71% BRING: torkoal, 15% BRING: scrafty, 8% BRING: alcremierubyswirl

Incineroar gives Intimidate and Fake Out support against the physical threats. Garchomp is fast and hits Torkoal and Appletun hard, and Gholdengo covers Alcremie and Torkoal with strong special attacks. This trio covers the most of their team.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick 3 from our team against their lineup of rotom, torkoal, torterra, scrafty, alcremie, and appletun. Looking at the matchups, Torterra, Appletun, and Torkoal with drought seem like the biggest threats, while Rotom, Scrafty, and Alcremie round out their coverage. From our side, Incineroar's intimidate and fake out utility plus Garchomp's strength against Torkoal stand out as good picks.

Kingambit doesn't do much against Scrafty since Fighting resists Dark. Archaludon's Steel typing is super effective against Alcremie's Fairy but weak against Torkoal's Fire. Sinistcha struggles against Torterra's Grass typing but its Ghost-type move could hit Rotom super effectively.

I'm settling on Incineroar for support with Intimidate and Fake Out, Garchomp for its Earthquake sweeping Torkoal super effectively while outspeeding it, and Gholdengo for special coverage against the rest of the team—a solid trio covering Fire, Dragon, and Fighting angles.

decisions.thought: 46% SWITCH: torkoal, 19% MOVE: discharge, 11% MOVE: charge

Fake Out is useless here because Rotom is Ghost-type and immune to Normal moves. Rotom is faster and already at -1 Attack, so Flare Blitz is the strongest damaging option that keeps Incineroar on the field.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Rotom is Electric/Ghost, so Fake Out being Normal-type won't land. Flare Blitz is Fire though, which hits Rotom neutrally regardless of its specific form, so that's a viable option instead.

I'm also weighing Parting Shot to pivot into Gholdengo, since Shadow Ball from Gholdengo would hit Rotom's Ghost typing super effectively, though I need to check how Rotom's Electric STAB interacts with Gholdengo's Steel typing in return.

Given Rotom's Attack is already lowered and Incineroar has solid bulk, I'll just stick with Flare Blitz for reliable damage here rather than switching.

decisions.thought: 24% SWITCH: rotom, 23% MOVE: flamethrower, 21% MOVE: flamecharge

Flare Blitz is resisted by Fire-type Torkoal, so it's a poor trade. Parting Shot cuts Torkoal's Attack and Sp. Atk while Incineroar switches out. Garchomp can then come in: it resists Fire, outspeeds Torkoal, and Earthquake hits hard.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Torkoal is the opponent's active Pokémon, a Fire-type that resists Flare Blitz, so I need to consider other options against it rather than attacking with a resisted move.

Parting Shot lets me pivot Incineroar out safely while debuffing Torkoal's attack and special attack. Garchomp would be a great switch-in since Dragon/Ground resists Fire and outspeeds Torkoal, letting it threaten with Earthquake.

decisions.thought: Only two switches are legal, and Incineroar is about to be hit by Rotom, which outspeeds it. Gholdengo's Shadow Ball is super effective against Rotom's Ghost typing, and Rotom is already at -1 SpA, so Gholdengo is the stronger switch-in. Garchomp's Ground moves are useless into levitate.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since only switching is allowed with Incineroar active, I need to decide between Garchomp and Gholdengo against the opposing Rotom, which is Electric/Ghost-typed—checking whether Ghost-type moves like Shadow Ball would be effective against it given its typing.

Gholdengo's Shadow Ball hits Rotom super effectively, and while Garchomp's Ground moves are useless against Levitate-immune Rotom, Gholdengo with Life Orb has decent speed and offers the better matchup here—I'll switch to Gholdengo.

decisions.thought: 51% SWITCH: torkoal, 16% MOVE: discharge, 11% MOVE: charge

Rotom is Electric/Ghost, so Shadow Ball is super effective and Gholdengo's 203 SpA with Life Orb makes it the strongest hit. Make It Rain and Thunderbolt are resisted, and Make It Rain would also drop Gholdengo's Sp. Atk by 2. Shadow Ball is the clear choice.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Rotom is Electric/Ghost, so Shadow Ball hits it super effectively. With Gholdengo's high SpA and Life Orb boosting damage, Shadow Ball against a weakened Rotom at -1 SpA should deal heavy damage, likely close to a OHKO.

decisions.thought: 29% MOVE: discharge, 22% MOVE: doubleteam, 22% MOVE: charge

Rotom is Electric/Ghost, so Shadow Ball is super effective, and Gholdengo's 203 Sp. Atk with Life Orb should knock it out. Gholdengo is also faster than Rotom's possible range would need to be to matter here, so it likely hits first anyway. Shadow Ball is the clear choice.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Rotom's Electric/Ghost typing takes super-effective damage from Shadow Ball, and with Gholdengo's high SpA plus Life Orb boost, Shadow Ball should deal heavy damage against Rotom's SpD, likely close to a KO given Rotom's HP range.

decisions.thought: 34% MOVE: bulldoze, 33% MOVE: shellsmash, 18% MOVE: bulletseed

Torterra is Grass/Ground, so Thunderbolt does nothing. Gholdengo outspeeds it (136 vs 68-118), and Shadow Ball is neutral with STAB and Life Orb for roughly half of Torterra's HP. Make It Rain would drop Gholdengo's Sp. Atk by 2, so Shadow Ball is the clean damage option.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking Gholdengo's move options against Torterra's Grass/Ground typing — Shadow Ball hits neutrally, while Make It Rain's Steel typing isn't resisted by Grass either, so I need to figure out which deals more damage.

Running the numbers, Shadow Ball with STAB and Life Orb against Torterra's likely Defense looks like roughly 50-55% damage, while Make It Rain hits harder but tanks Gholdengo's Special Attack by two stages afterward. Thunderbolt is useless since Ground types are immune to Electric, so I'm leaning toward Shadow Ball as the safer, repeatable option given Torterra's threatening Ground/Grass STAB moves like Earthquake or Wood Hammer.

decisions.thought: 27% MOVE: bulldoze, 25% MOVE: seedbomb, 25% MOVE: shellsmash

Gholdengo has 6 HP, so any hit kills it, and it may be slower than Torterra (68-118 Spe vs its -1 ~91). Incineroar's Intimidate weakens Torterra's Bulldoze on entry, and Flare Blitz is super effective on the Grass/Ground Torterra at 41% HP. Switching in gives the more reliable knockout.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Gholdengo is nearly dead at 6 HP while Torterra sits at 41%. Since Torterra has no weakness to Ghost, a Shadow Ball from Gholdengo with its boosted Special Attack and Life Orb would deal roughly 75 HP worth of damage, leaving Torterra still standing at a reduced health total.

The recoil from Life Orb would faint Gholdengo regardless of whether it lands the KO on Torterra, since that recoil applies even on a successful knockout. Speed matters here too—if Torterra moves first, it could use Bulldoze to finish Gholdengo off before it even attacks, while Thunderbolt from Gholdengo would be useless against Torterra's Ground typing. Shadow Ball remains the best offensive option over Make It Rain given the typing matchup, though switching out is also worth considering.

Switching to Incineroar is tempting since Flare Blitz would hit Torterra super effectively through its Grass typing, and Incineroar can tank the incoming Bulldoze without issue. The question is whether Incineroar outspeeds Torterra's wide speed range to land that KO, versus just using Gholdengo's Shadow Ball now while its uncertain speed tier might still let it move first.

Given Incineroar's intimidate softens the Bulldoze hit and it likely survives to deliver a near-guaranteed Flare Blitz KO afterward, switching to Incineroar seems like the safer, more reliable play compared to gambling on Gholdengo's fragile 6 HP and speed tie.

decisions.thought: 32% MOVE: seedbomb, 29% MOVE: shellsmash, 20% MOVE: bulldoze
Torterra is at 41% and is faster than my -1 Incineroar, but Flare Blitz is super effective and should easily knock it out. Incineroar at 114 HP should survive a Bulldoze hit first.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's Flare Blitz hits for super effective damage against Torterra's Grass typing, and with Torterra already at 41% HP (~76 out of 186), I'm checking if this 120 BP move with Incineroar's 183 Attack against Torterra's defense around 140 is enough to knock it out.

Running the numbers, Flare Blitz with STAB and the type effectiveness bonus lands well over 200 damage, far exceeding Torterra's remaining HP for a clean knockout. Torterra is faster and could try Bulldoze for neutral damage against Incineroar, but it won't be enough to prevent the KO from Flare Blitz, so that's the clear choice here.
